title.es: Simulación de una reunión de vecinos

es: Participar en una reunión simulada de vecinos: proponer, conceder un punto, discrepar con tacto y llegar a un acuerdo.

teaching.en: I'd like to propose a small garden next to the school.
teaching.es: Me gustaría proponer un pequeño huerto junto a la escuela.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd like to propose + nombre: propuesta formal y cortés para abrir un punto en una reunión.
segments: I'd like to propose a small
teaching.audioText: I'd like to propose a small garden next to the school.

teaching.en: Admittedly, it would cost more, but it would last longer.
teaching.es: Es cierto que costaría más, pero duraría más.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly concede un punto contrario antes de defender tu idea con but.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, it would cost more, but it would last longer.

teaching.en: With respect, I see it a little differently.
teaching.es: Con todo respeto, yo lo veo un poco distinto.
teaching.explanationEs: With respect suaviza el desacuerdo; a little differently evita decir «estás equivocado».
teaching.audioText: With respect, I see it a little differently.

teaching.en: I understand your concern, but I'm not sure it would work.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu preocupación, pero no estoy seguro de que funcione.
teaching.explanationEs: Reconoce el problema y expresa duda con I'm not sure: discrepancia con tacto.

teaching.audioText: I understand your concern, but I'm not sure it would work.

teaching.en: Shall we agree to start small and review the cost in June?
teaching.es: ¿Acordamos empezar poco a poco y revisar el coste en junio?
teaching.explanationEs: Shall we agree to + verbo propone un acuerdo y deja la decisión al grupo.

and review the cost in June?
teaching.audioText: Shall we agree to start small and review the cost in June?

teaching.en: To sum up, we agree on the garden and will review the budget in June.
teaching.es: En resumen, estamos de acuerdo con el huerto y revisaremos el presupuesto en junio.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up cierra la reunión repitiendo lo acordado.

and will review the budget in June.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que hace una propuesta cortés a los vecinos.

choices.text: You must build a garden by the school.
A garden is the only option.
I'd like to propose a small garden by the school.

feedback.es: I'd like to propose + nombre abre una propuesta con cortesía; las otras opciones imponen o cierran el debate.

hint.es: Busca la que empieza con I'd like to propose.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es cierto que el plan es difícil, pero es justo.»

feedback.es: Admittedly concede la dificultad antes de defender que el plan es justo.

hint.es: Es el adverbio de concesión que significa «es cierto que».

origin.text: ___, the plan is difficult, but it is fair.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Podríamos acordar probarlo durante tres meses.»

answer.text: Could we agree to try it for three months

feedback.es: Could we agree to + verbo propone un acuerdo con plazo y deja abierta la respuesta.

hint.es: Empieza con Could we agree to.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su jugada en la reunión.

pairs: What if we try a weekly market?
With respect, I see it differently.
Shall we agree to try it for a month?

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una jugada: What if… propone, Admittedly concede, With respect discrepa con tacto y Shall we agree cierra el acuerdo.

pairs: What if we try a weekly market?
With respect, I see it differently.
Shall we agree to try it for a month?

prompt.es: Escucha a la vecina y elige qué hace.

choices.text: She disagrees politely and offers another idea.
She agrees completely and ends the discussion.
She refuses to talk about the noise.

feedback.es: I take your point concede la preocupación, pero I'm not sure… discrepa y Perhaps we could… ofrece otra idea.

origin.audio: I take your point about the noise, but I'm not sure a later closing time would solve it. Perhaps we could ask the café to close at ten.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta cortés a una propuesta que no te convence.

choices.text: That is a terrible idea. Nobody wants noise.
I like the idea, but I'm a bit worried about the noise.
Fine. Do what you want.

feedback.es: I like the idea, but I'm a bit worried… reconoce la idea y expresa la duda con un atenuador; las otras opciones son bruscas o evasivas.

origin.text: Tom proposes a concert in the park every Friday. You think it would be too noisy.

prompt.es: Elige el cierre que resume el acuerdo de la reunión.

choices.text: To sum up, we disagree about the market and will not meet again.
To sum up, the market will open every day from July.
To sum up, we agree to try a small market for a month and meet again in July.

feedback.es: To sum up repite lo acordado: mercado pequeño, prueba de un mes y nueva reunión en julio.

origin.text: After the meeting, the neighbours will start a small market, try it for a month and meet again in July.

prompt.es: Escucha a la vecina y elige qué concede y qué propone.

choices.text: She admits a point, but proposes a shorter test.
She rejects any test and ends the talk.
She accepts a longer test without changes.

feedback.es: Admittedly concede que una prueba larga sería más barata, y What if we agree on six weeks? propone una prueba más corta.

origin.audio: Admittedly, a longer test would be cheaper for us, but I'm afraid the café can't wait. What if we agree on six weeks?

prompt.es: Completa: «Con todo respeto, yo lo veo de otra manera.»

feedback.es: With respect es la fórmula cortés para discrepar sin atacar.

origin.text: With ___, I see it a little differently.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: propón, concede, discrepa con tacto y acuerda.

answer.text: Thank you, everyone. I would like to propose a street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants. It would bring neighbours together and help small businesses. Tom, I take your point: admittedly, a market may be noisy, and we do not have much money. However, I see it a little differently. With respect, I think the noise would last only a few hours, and the stall fees could pay for the cleaning. I'm afraid I cannot agree that the risk is so big. Could we agree to try it for one month and then review the noise and the cost together? If it does not work, we will stop. Shall we say that we start in October and meet again in November?
accepted: Thank you, everyone. I would like to propose a street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants. It would bring neighbours together and help small businesses. Tom, I take your point: admittedly, a market may be noisy, and we do not have much money. However, I see it a little differently. With respect, I think the noise would last only a few hours, and the stall fees could pay for the cleaning. I'm afraid I cannot agree that the risk is so big. Could we agree to try it for one month and then review the noise and the cost together? If it does not work, we will stop. Shall we say that we start in October and meet again in November?

Good evening. I'd like to suggest closing our street to cars on one Sunday a month for a small market. It is true that it could be loud, Tom, and I understand your worry about the budget. Still, I am not sure that the problem is as big as it seems. The stalls would pay a small fee, and volunteers could help clean the street afterwards. What if we agree to a one-month test? Perhaps we could meet again afterwards and decide together whether the market should continue. I believe this is fair for everyone, and I hope you agree.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención propone el mercado, concede un punto a Tom, discrepa con tacto y cierra con un acuerdo de prueba concreto.

origin.text: Reunión de vecinos. Propones cerrar una calle un domingo al mes para un mercado. Tom cree que habrá demasiado ruido y que faltará dinero. Escribe entre 90 y 130 palabras: propón el mercado, concede un punto a Tom, discrepa con tacto y propón un acuerdo final (prueba de un mes).

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase concede un punto sin cerrar la discusión?

choices.text: You are wrong, and that is final.
I take your point, but let's look at the cost again.
I don't care about the cost.

feedback.es: I take your point reconoce lo dicho y but let's look at the cost again mantiene la conversación abierta; las otras opciones cierran el tema.

origin.text: Tom says the cost is too high. You want to keep talking without being rude.

prompt.es: Escucha el final de la reunión y elige qué hará Mia.

choices.text: She will buy the paint.
She will paint the gate alone.
She will look for helpers.

feedback.es: Mia dice que buscará voluntarios; Tom comprará la pintura.

origin.audio: To sum up, we agree to paint the gate in May. Tom will buy the paint, and Mia will ask for volunteers.
